markscheme.marking_summary: Exact original MS leaf excerpt: Award [3] max Award [1] per point Initial State: Before payment, the patient's account shows a due balance; Transition State: During payment processing, the system temporarily locks the patient's record to update payment details; Final State: After successful payment, the new balance is shown, often updating the patient's status to 'Paid' or 'Cleared'; Error Handling: In case of transaction failure, the system rolls back to the initial state, ensuring data integrity; Note: Accept alternative terminology e.g. consistent, intermediate, and final.

markscheme.marking_summary: Exact original MS leaf excerpt: Award [3] max Award [1] per point a consistent version of the DB is recovered from backup; the log file is scanned to determine the most recent checkpoint; the committed and uncommitted transactions (since that checkpoint) are determined; the committed transactions are redone (reapplied to the database); the uncommitted transactions are undone / rollback (in the case of immediate update);

practice_questions.question_text: A museum has many departments. Each curator and each technician belongs to one department. A curator can work with several technicians, and a technician can work with several curators. Construct an ERD showing these three relationships and their cardinalities.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: DEPARTMENT 1—many CURATOR; DEPARTMENT 1—many TECHNICIAN; CURATOR many—many TECHNICIAN. A link entity may resolve the last relationship.

marking_points.criterion: Curator to technician is many-to-many, or correct link-entity resolution.

practice_questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of replacing separate paper equipment logs with a shared relational database used by several museum departments. Develop each benefit in this setting.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution: Concurrency control lets staff record loans simultaneously while preventing conflicting updates, so separate departments see consistent equipment availability. Queries can retrieve overdue equipment by borrower and date quickly, avoiding manual searches and helping staff recover items before another booking.

marking_points.criterion: Explains borrower/date query compared with manual search.

acceptable_alternatives: Accept two other developed relational-database benefits supported by A3.1.1, with distinct consequences.

practice_questions.question_text: A transaction transfers an item from store A to store B by decreasing A’s count and increasing B’s count. Describe the database state before the transaction, during its updates, and after a successful COMMIT.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Uses the explicit 2027 commit/transaction scope rather than requiring an old named transaction-state taxonomy.
practice_questions.solution: Before it begins, both counts satisfy the inventory rules. During the transaction, one update may have occurred while the other is pending; those partial changes must not be treated as a completed transfer. COMMIT makes both changes durable together, leaving a consistent inventory total.

marking_points.criterion: Intermediate partial updates are not a completed transfer.
Commit preserves both updates and restores the required consistent total.

practice_questions.partial_credit_notes: Award independent criteria up to the stated total; accept equivalent technically correct wording/solutions.

verification.technical: Concrete answer reasoned and checked against full syllabus guidance and available source MS.

practice_questions.question_text: A transaction has decreased store A’s count but fails before increasing store B’s count. Describe how ROLLBACK should affect the transaction and the inventory total.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Retains undo/recovery reasoning through explicit ROLLBACK; log/checkpoint recovery algorithms are not claimed as requirements.
practice_questions.solution: It undoes the uncommitted decrease at A. Neither half of the failed transfer remains, so the counts return to their prior consistent values and no item disappears from the inventory.

practice_questions.question_text: MEASUREMENT uses (DeviceID, SensorID, Timestamp) as a composite primary key. Outline why Timestamp may be needed when the same sensor measures the same device repeatedly.

practice_questions.solution: DeviceID and SensorID repeat for successive measurements. Timestamp distinguishes those events so separate readings can be stored without duplicate keys.

practice_questions.question_text: READING(DeviceID, TechID, RecordedAt) and TECHNICIAN(TechID, Name) use ISO date-time strings. Construct SQL listing device IDs read by R. Kim at any time on 12 May 2027.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Rebuilt scenario and response wording while retaining the supported reasoning; source-specific obsolete material excluded.
practice_questions.solution:
One solution:
SELECT r.DeviceID FROM Reading r JOIN Technician t ON r.TechID=t.TechID WHERE t.Name='R. Kim' AND r.RecordedAt >= '2027-05-12 00:00' AND r.RecordedAt < '2027-05-13 00:00';

marking_points.criterion: Includes the whole specified day and excludes other days.
